From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@hyperlytics.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + benchmark download — quick demo?

Hi Rachel,

I just downloaded the Redwood benchmark report last night (great work — appreciate the latency breakdowns). My team at Hyperlytics is evaluating inference options for our analytics pipeline and I wanted to see a quick product walkthrough focused on cost/throughput tradeoffs for long-context extraction.

Would you or someone on your team be available for a 30-min demo next week? We are on Pacific time. Best windows for us: Tue/Wed afternoon (1–4pm PT).

I attached the benchmark snapshot we generated from our side that highlights our sequence length distribution. Happy to send more context if useful.

Thanks,
Oliver Grant
Director of Data Platforms
Hyperlytics

Attachment: hyperlytics-benchmark-20260629.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB)

Hi Oliver — thanks for downloading the report and for sending your benchmark snapshot. I'm Rachel on the solutions team; copying Dylan (SDR) so he can help with calendar coordination.

We'd love to walk through how Redwood can optimize cost for long-context workloads and show a few examples of autoscaling and KV/prefix caching that are relevant to your profile.

Proposed 30-min slots (PT):
- Tue 2026-07-07 13:30–14:00
- Tue 2026-07-07 15:00–15:30
- Wed 2026-07-08 14:00–14:30

If none of those work, tell us a preferred day/time range and we'll accommodate. Also, any specific question we should prep for (quantization, on-prem deployment, or SLOs)?

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

--
Rachel Kim
Redwood Inference

Hi Rachel — thanks, those slots look good. We can do Tue 2026-07-07 15:00–15:30 PT. Please lock that in.

For the agenda: 1) quick platform overview (10 min) 2) cost/throughput examples for long-context extractions (10 min) 3) next steps and a short mutual action plan (10 min).

A couple quick notes from our side: we regularly push batches of 20–30 long documents (avg 8k tokens) and are sensitive to tail latency. We are particularly curious about the caching + KV behavior you mention in the benchmark.

Oliver
